title: ADAPTIVE USER INTERFACES FOR BRAIN COMPUTER INTERFACE SYSTEMS
abstract: The present disclosure relates to systems and method for adapting a brain-computer interface to a user. In some aspects, the method includes providing an electronic user interface of a brain-computer interface configured to interact with an electronic device using a plurality of electronic control switches selectable using a neural activity of the user. The electronic user interface may be configured to increase or decrease a complexity level of a display of one or more of the plurality electronic control switches displayed by the user interface. The method may include adjusting the complexity level of the display based on monitoring the user, monitoring electronic testing activity of the user, or monitoring parameters associated with the user to establish an ability level of the user.
first_claim: 1. A method of adapting a brain-computer interface, comprising: providing a display on an electronic user interface operative with the brain-computer interface, wherein the display comprises a plurality of electronic control switches selectable using a neural activity of a user, and wherein the electronic user interface can adjust a complexity level of the display; providing an electronic testing activity for the neural activity on the electronic user interface; and adjusting the complexity level of the display based at least in part on a result of the electronic testing activity.

title: CONTEXTUALIZED DECODING FOR BRAIN COMPUTER INTERFACE SYSTEMS
abstract: Decoders for brain-computer interfaces (BCI) contextually decode a neural signal from an individual to produce an actionable command that allows the BCI to interact with one or more electronic devices. A neural interface device implanted in proximity to an individual’s motor cortex generates an electronic signal representative of brain activity, which is transmitted to a computer processor. The computer processor receives non-neural user interface (UI) state data reflecting a state of a computer application on an electronic device operably connected to the BCI, and uses a decoding model to automatically decode the electronic signal into an output signal based at least in part on the non-neural UI state data, including by selecting a decoding option based on comparative accuracy and speed. The output signal is transmitted to the electronic device to allow the individual to interact with it using brain activity.
first_claim: 1. A method of interacting with one or more electronic devices using brain activity of an individual implanted with a neural interface device, the method comprising: generating an electronic signal by the neural interface device implanted in proximity to a motor cortex of the individual; transmitting the electronic signal to a computer processor; receiving non-neural user interface (UI) state data at the computer processor, wherein the non-neural UI state data is separate from the electronic signal and comprises user interface state information of a computer application of the one or more electronic devices, the one or more electronic devices operably connected to a brain computer interface; automatically decoding, by a decoding model, the electronic signal to produce an output signal, wherein the output signal is based at least in part on the non-neural UI state data; and electronically transmitting the output signal to the one or more electronic devices operably connected to the brain computer interface.

title: ENHANCEMENT OF BLOOD BRAIN BARRIER PERMEABILITY WITH LOW INTENSITY AND VARIABLE FREQUENCY MAGNETIC STIMULATION
abstract: The present disclosure provides, in part, methods of transient blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption by applying repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) therapy to a subject in need thereof for central nervous system (CNS)-targeted drug delivery. The present disclosure also provides, in part, devices that generate a low intensity magnetic field and variable frequencies for rTMS.
first_claim: 1. A repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) method for central nervous system (CNS)-targeted drug delivery, comprising repetitively applying a magnetic pulse with one or more coils configured to emit a magnetic field through a surface of the head of a subject in need thereof, thereby affecting tight junctions of microvascular endothelial cells in at least a portion of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), and transiently opening and/or disrupting at least a portion of the BBB, wherein the magnetic pulse is applied: at a frequency of about or at least about 10 Hz to about or at least about 500,000 Hz; and at an intensity of about or at least about 0.0005 to about or at least about 0.1 Tesla.

title: METHODS AND DEVICES FOR SUPERVISION OF CLOSED-LOOP NEURAL STIMULATION THERAPY
abstract: Methods and systems for adapting a neuromodulation system to changes in system integrity. A system may check system integrity in response to the passage of time or to an asynchronous trigger. If a loss of system integrity is identified, changes to therapy program parameters are determined and tested for satisfactory performance. The changes to a therapy program may include identifying a new therapeutic target. Physician approval of the change process, as well as final program parameters, is contemplated.
first_claim: 1. An implantable device for controllably delivering neural stimuli, the device comprising: a pulse generator configured to deliver neural stimuli via one or more stimulation electrodes to a neural pathway, the neural stimuli being configured to evoke neural responses from the neural pathway; measurement circuitry configured to capture signal windows from signals sensed on the neural pathway by one or more measurement electrodes; and a controller configured to: control the pulse generator to deliver a neural stimulus according to a stimulus intensity; measure a characteristic of an evoked neural response in a captured signal window subsequent to the neural stimulus; determine a feedback variable from the measured characteristic of the evoked neural response; and adjust, using a feedback controller, the stimulus intensity so as to maintain the feedback variable at or near a target value; and a supervisor configured to: in response to determining that an out-of-compliance (OOC) event is occurring, configure the feedback controller to determine the stimulus intensity so as to not exceed a compliant stimulus intensity.

title: METHODS AND SYSTEMS FOR AUTOMATED CALIBRATION OF LOCAL FIELD POTENTIAL SENSING TOOLS FOR DEEP BRAIN STIMULATION
abstract: A system for automated calibration of Local Field Potential (LFP) sensing for deep brain stimulation can comprise one or more electrodes and control circuitry. The control circuitry is configured to, prior to delivery of electrical stimulation via the one or more electrodes, sense, using the one or more electrodes, LFPs of the brain, record a snapshot of LFP activity across a wide frequency band, determine a peak frequency of the LFP activity from the snapshot, and update a Frequency of Interest (FOI) based on the peak frequency.
first_claim: 1. A system for automated calibration of Local Field Potential (LFP) sensing for deep brain stimulation comprising: one or more electrodes; control circuitry configured to, prior to delivery of electrical stimulation via the one or more electrodes: sense, using the one or more electrodes, LFPs of the brain; record a snapshot of LFP wide-band activity; determine a peak frequency of the LFP wide-band activity from the snapshot; and update a Frequency of Interest (FOI) based on the peak frequency.

title: System and method for deep brain stimulation
abstract: A cystoscopy system with intracranial electrodes operable to be disposed in a hippocampus region of a brain and configured to record electrical signals that include biomarkers related to memory encoding, a neurostimulator configured to stimulate a posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) of the brain, a NARXNN plant model, and a controller configured to receive the electrical signals and modulate an input/output (I/O) relationship between the biomarkers and electrical stimuli applied to a posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) of the brain by controlling the neurostimulator to stimulate the PCC based on the I/O relationship to achieve a desired level of the biomarkers.
first_claim: 1. A system for deep brain stimulation, the system comprising: intracranial electrodes operable to be disposed in a hippocampus region of a brain and configured to record electrical signals; a signal processor configured to denoise the electrical signals and process the electrical signals to extract biomarkers from the electrical signals, the biomarkers related to memory encoding; a neurostimulator configured to stimulate a posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) of the brain; and a controller configured to receive the biomarkers and modulate an input/output (I/O) relationship between the biomarkers and electrical stimuli applied to the (PCC) of the brain by controlling the neurostimulator to stimulate the PCC based on the I/O relationship to achieve a desired level of the biomarkers.
assignees: THE BOARD OF REGENTS OF THE UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS SYSTEM

title: Graphene-based electrodes for electroencephalogram-based brain computer interface systems
abstract: A brain-computer interface (BCI) system that includes a cap having wired electrodes selected such as a graphene-based electrode and a reduced graphene oxide (rGO)-coated electrode; a data acquisition and processing unit; and a computing device. The cap is operatively connected to the data acquisition and processing unit via the wired electrodes. The computing device has a communications interface coupled to the data acquisition and processing unit. A method of recording and monitoring brain activities of a subject via the BCI system. A method of making the graphene-based electrode and the reduced graphene oxide (rGO)-coated electrode.
first_claim: 1. A brain-computer interface (BCI) system, comprising: a cap comprising a plurality of wired electrodes, wherein the wired electrodes comprises at least one electrode selected from the group consisting of a graphene-coated electrode and a reduced graphene oxide (rGO)-coated electrode, and further comprise polypyrrole that is homogenously mixed with graphene or rGO, and wherein each electrode of the wired electrodes comprises a repeating pattern of etchings, trenches or concaves that extend below a surface, and graphene and/or rGO are uniformly coated both on the surface and within the pattern; a data acquisition and processing unit; wherein the cap is operatively connected to the data acquisition and processing unit via the plurality of wired electrodes; and a computing device, wherein the computing device has a communications interface coupled to the data acquisition and processing unit; wherein the BCI system removably retains the computing device; wherein the plurality of wired electrodes is configured to detect one or more electroencephalograph (EEG) signals from a plurality of brain areas of the subject wearing the cap; wherein the data acquisition and processing unit is configured to characterize brain activities of the subject based on the one or more EEG signals transmitted from the plurality of wired electrodes; and wherein each EEG signal of the one or more EEG signals corresponds to the brain activities of the subject.

title: Protocol to enhance therapeutic effects of transcranial magnetic stimulation
abstract: A system for administering transcranial magnetic stimulation to a subject is provided. The system includes a coil a controller, and a high-power switching module. The controller is configured to generate low voltage control signals for administering a treatment protocol via the coil. The high-power switching module is configured to generate a high voltage current delivered to the coil based on the low voltage control signals. In some embodiments, the high-power switching module includes a printed circuit board used to reduce intrinsic resistance and parasitic capacitance of the circuit such that the current delivered to the coil over a sequence of bursts remains stable. A new protocol for administering transcranial magnetic stimulation, referred to as high-density Theta Burst Stimulation (hdTBS), utilizes a pulse frequency of at least 40 Hz and a number of pulses per burst of four or greater.
first_claim: 1. A system for administering transcranial magnetic stimulation, the system comprising: a coil; a controller configured to generate low voltage control signals; and a high-power switching circuit configured to generate a high voltage current delivered to the coil based on the low voltage control signals: wherein the high-power switching circuit comprises a first portion and a second portion, wherein the first portion includes a first power supply unit, a first capacitor, and a first insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT), wherein the second portion includes a second power supply unit, a second capacitor, and a second IGBT, and wherein the first power supply unit is connected in series with the second power supply unit; wherein the first power supply unit is connected in parallel with the first capacitor, and wherein the first power supply unit is connected in series with the first IGBT; wherein the second power supply unit is connected in parallel with the second capacitor, and wherein the second power supply unit is connected in series with the second IGBT; wherein the first IGBT and the second IGBT are configured to deliver biphasic pulses to the coil; and wherein the controller is configured to cause the high-power switching circuit to generate a plurality of bursts of pulses of current through the coil, wherein a pulse frequency of each burst of pulses is at least 40 Hz and a number of pulses per burst is at least four.
assignees: The United States of America, as represented by the Secretary, Department of Health and Human Services

title: SYSTEMS AND METHODS FOR TARGETED NEUROMODULATION
abstract: A system and a method for targeted neuromodulation are disclosed. The neuromodulation system comprises a wearable patch configured for placement on a target anatomical region of a user's body. The wearable patch comprises a microneedle array designed to deliver a medicament to neural tissue adjacent to the patch, one or more electrodes for delivering electrical stimulation to the neural tissue, and one or more biosensors for detecting pain-related biomarkers. A controller, operatively coupled to the microneedle array and the electrodes, is configured to adjust at least one of a medicament delivery rate and one or more electrical stimulation parameters in response to the detected pain-related biomarkers and a physiological condition. The system provides adaptive modulation of serotonergic pain pathways to mitigate postsurgical pain and prevent latent sensitization in patients, particularly those with a history of mild traumatic brain injury.
first_claim: 1. A neuromodulation system, comprising: a wearable patch configured for placement on a target anatomical region of a user's body; a microneedle array disposed on the wearable patch, the microneedle array configured to deliver a medicament to a neural tissue adjacent to the wearable patch; one or more electrodes integrated into the wearable patch, the one or more electrodes configured to deliver electrical stimulation to the neural tissue; one or more biosensors configured to detect one or more pain-related biomarkers; and a controller configured to: determine, based on the one or more pain-related biomarkers, whether a detected physiological condition corresponds to a pain-related condition; and adjust at least one of a medicament delivery rate and one or more electrical stimulation parameters in response to the determining.

title: SYSTEMS AND METHODS FOR MAGNETIC RESONANCE BASED SKULL THERMOMETRY
abstract: Described herein are systems, methods, and computer-readable medium for magnetic resonance (MR) based thermometry. A method for magnetic resonance based thermometry includes: acquiring, by a T1 mapping sequence, MR data in an area of interest of a subject that is heated by the application of focused ultrasound (FUS) to the brain of the subject, where the MR data includes T1 values over time, and where the acquisition of the MR data includes applying an accelerated three-dimensional ultra-short spiral acquisition sequence with a nonselective excitation pulse; tracking changes in proton resonance frequency and determining, based at least in part on a mathematical relationship established by T1 mapping thermometry, a temperature change in the area of interest over time, and where the temperature change is caused at least in part by a change in the applied FUS.
first_claim: 1. A method for magnetic resonance (MR) based thermometry, comprising: acquiring MR data in an area of cortical bone of at least part of a skull of a subject that is heated by application of focused ultrasound (FUS) to soft tissue of the subject, calculating a corresponding temperature change in the cortical bone by tracking changes in a proton resonance frequency (PRF) during the application of the focused ultrasound (FUS) to the soft tissue; wherein the MR data comprises a plurality of T1 values acquired over time in a computer implemented MR imaging acquisition sequence comprising steps of: applying a fat suppression pulse prior to applying a non-selective RF pulse that initiates the MR imaging acquisition sequence; applying an ultra-short (UTE) spiral acquisition sequence with the nonselective excitation pulse for acquiring bone image data; and applying a long echo time (LTE) spiral acquisition sequence with the non-selective excitation pulse for acquiring soft tissue image data; determining, based at least in part on a mathematical relationship established by T1 mapping thermometry and the changes in the proton resonance frequency (PRF), the corresponding temperature change in the cortical bone that occurs at least in part by a change in the application of the FUS.

title: Simultaneous focused ultrasound and fMRI and application of focused ultrasound outside of MRI environment
abstract: A workflow has been developed that enables initially mapping of a focused ultrasound (FUS) beam using magnetic resonance (MR) thermometry or MR-acoustic radiation force imaging (MR-ARFI) while working within the MRI device. During this procedure, key measurements will be taken including the precise location of the transducer relative to the skull and the transducer parameters (such as amplitudes and phases) required to place the ultrasound focus at the desired focal size and location in the skull. The anatomical measurements will be used to build a patient-specific, device-specific stereotactic frame to hold the transducer in the position relative to the skull and the aberration corrects will be applied. FUS therapy can then be delivered to the patient outside of the MR environment.
first_claim: 1. A method for applying focused ultrasound (FUS) to a patient, the method comprising: mapping a FUS beam in the patient inside a magnetic resonance (MR) environment, the mapping employing MR thermometry or MR-acoustic radiation force imaging (MR-ARFI); obtaining acoustic data during the mapping by recording at least radiofrequency (RF) echo signals resulting from the use of a FUS transducer or an array of FUS transducers positioned inside the MR environment and acoustic feedback from a reflection pattern of the patient as an acoustic signature of FUS transducer position relative to the patient; building a patient-specific stereotactic frame using the acoustic data obtained from the mapping; and after obtaining the acoustic data inside the MR environment, delivering FUS therapy to the patient outside of the MR environment using the patient-specific stereotactic frame and using the acoustic data, wherein delivering FUS therapy to the patient outside of the MR environment comprises comparing a current acoustic signature obtained outside of the MR environment with the acoustic signature obtained during the mapping inside the MR environment to confirm that the FUS transducer or the array of FUS transducers is positioned relative to the patient in a same orientation as during the mapping.

title: Automated selection of electrodes and stimulation parameters in a deep brain stimulation system using anatomical structures
abstract: A method for optimizing stimulation for a patient having a stimulator device such as a Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) device is disclosed, which involves a consideration of tissue imaging information in the environment around the lead. Test stimulation is provided at initial combinations of lead positions and values of a stimulation parameter such as amplitude, with patient results scored for each combination. Tissue imaging information is assessed in conjunction with these scores, and a next combination of position and a value of the stimulation parameter to test is determined. This process repeats iteratively until a stopping criterium is met. The lead positions in question may be longitudinal or rotational positions around the lead, and preferably both if the lead is directional in nature. Tissue imaging information can also be used to exclude certain positions or stimulation values during subsequent optimization testing.
first_claim: 1. A method for optimizing stimulation for a patient having a stimulator device, wherein the stimulator device comprises a plurality of electrodes in an electrode array for providing stimulation, the method providing test stimulation at a plurality of different combinations of a position in the electrode array and a value of at least one stimulation parameter, the method comprising: (a) receiving imaging information from an external system about tissue structures surrounding the electrode array; (b) processing the imaging information to determine a first data set comprising values each indicative of a desirability of providing stimulation at a possible one of the combinations; (c) executing an algorithm to provide test stimulation at a plurality of the combinations, wherein the algorithm iteratively determines a next combination to test using at least one score for each previously tested combination and the first data set; and (d) using the scores at the tested combinations to determine an optimal therapeutic stimulation for the patient.

title: DEEP BRAIN STIMULATION SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR AUTOMATIC ADJUSTMENT OF STIMULATION VIA WORKLOAD MEASURE INTERPRETATION
abstract: A system and method are provided that receive physiological data of a patient measured by physiological sensor(s). A workload measurement is selected based on the physiological data that is measured, patient subjective ratings of workload during performance of tests, and/or performance data provided by a physician during the tests. The workload measurement is selected from plural different values of the workload measurement, with the different values associated with (a) different sets of the physiological data of the patient previously measured during performance of designated physical tasks by the patient and (b) patient reported outcomes provided by the patient and indicative of perception by the patient of workload demands in completing the designated physical tasks. A level of DBS therapy delivered to the patient is automatically adjusted using an IPG based on the workload measurement that is selected.
first_claim: 1. A method of operating a deep brain stimulation (DBS) system to treat a neurological disorder of a patient, the method comprising: receiving physiological data of a patient measured by one or more physiological sensors; selecting a workload measurement based on the physiological data that is measured, the workload measurement selected from plural different values of the workload measurement associated with (a) different sets of the physiological data of the patient previously measured during performance of designated physical tasks by the patient and (b) patient reported outcomes provided by the patient and indicative of perception by the patient of workload demands in completing the designated physical tasks; adjusting, based on the selected workload measurement, one or more DBS operating parameters used by an implantable pulse generator (IPG) to deliver electrical stimulation therapy to a brain region of the patient, the one or more DBS operating parameters including at least one of a stimulation amplitude, pulse width, pulse frequency, duty cycle, stimulation program, or active electrode selection; and automatically causing the IPG to deliver DBS therapy according to the one or more DBS operating parameters that are adjusted.

title: Hiatal Hernia Procedure Combined with an Implanted Electrical Stimulation System to Treat Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease
abstract: Obligatory circumferential hiatal dissection with routine cruroplasty and crural closure mechanically anchors the GEJ intraabdominally via lead implant, combined with LES electrical stimulation, yielding durable reductions in esophageal acid exposure and GERD symptoms. This restores three anti-reflux mechanisms: intrinsic LES function via neuromodulation; extrinsic crural function via hiatal repair regardless of hernia; and GEJ position via dissection/lead fixation. The lead serves dually as conductor and anchor, resisting LES cephalad migration, preventing crural-LES separation during transient relaxations/swallowing, and potentially curbing post-op hiatal hernia recurrence. Staged activation lets surgical/anchoring effects mature pre-stimulation. Disclosed methods, systems, and claims encompass the three-mechanism platform, esophageal foreshortening embodiments, EGJ-CI-based selection, GEJ morphology classification, impedance-pH assessment, hiatal sac excision, acid pocket reduction, wireless reprogramming, and reversible operation.
first_claim: 1. A system for treating gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), comprising: an implantable pulse generator configured to generate electrical stimulation pulses; an implantable stimulation lead having a proximal portion electrically coupled to the implantable pulse generator and a distal electrode portion configured for implantation proximate a lower esophageal sphincter (LES); and at least one fixation member coupled to the stimulation lead and configured for fixation at or near a diaphragmatic hiatus, wherein the stimulation lead is configured to extend along a longitudinal axis of a distal esophagus when implanted, the fixation member is configured to maintain the LES and a gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) in an intra-abdominal position by resisting cephalad migration of the LES during esophageal foreshortening and the implantable pulse generator is configured to deliver electrical stimulation to the LES to increase an intrinsic LES function, such that the system is configured to simultaneously a) improve the intrinsic LES function, b) cooperate with a crural repair to support an extrinsic crural sphincter function, and c) maintain an intra-abdominal positioning of the LES and/or GEJ.

title: Neuromodulation to target glucose transporter and/or incretin pathways
abstract: The subject matter of the present disclosure generally relates to techniques for neuromodulation that include applying energy (e.g., ultrasound energy) into the tissue to cause a change in a glucose transporter pathway molecule and/or an incretin pathway molecule. In one embodiment, the neuromodulation is performed as a treatment of a metabolic disorder.
first_claim: 1. A method for treating a subject having a metabolic disorder, comprising: applying ultrasound energy to only a subregion of a liver, wherein the subregion comprises a porta hepatis of the liver and stimulating sensory neurons within an internal tissue of the subject to cause a change to a glucose transporter pathway molecule and/or an incretin pathway molecule in the subject to treat the metabolic disorder, wherein the ultrasound energy is applied by an extracorporeal energy application device, and wherein the change of the glucose transporter pathway molecule and/or incretin pathway molecule is at an internal organ that is distal from the internal tissue.

title: Controlling operation of a GPU
abstract: The operation of a GPU is controlled based on one or more deadlines by which one or more GPU tasks must be completed and estimates of the time required to complete the execution of a first GPU task (which is currently being executed) and the time required to execute one or more other GPU tasks (which are not currently being executed). Based on a comparison between the deadline(s) and the estimates, the operating parameters of the GPU may be changed.
first_claim: 1. A method of controlling operation of a GPU, the method comprising: identifying a set of GPU tasks, the set of GPU tasks comprising a plurality of GPU tasks; estimating a completion time for each of the GPU tasks in the set of GPU tasks; determining, using the estimated completion times, whether each GPU task in the set of GPU tasks can be completed before a deadline associated with a particular GPU task; and in response to determining that all the GPU tasks in the set of GPU tasks cannot be completed before their associated deadlines, changing the operation of the GPU to increase an operating frequency of the GPU.

title: GPU-BASED QUERY PROCESSING ACCELERATION METHOD AND COMPUTING SYSTEM
abstract: A method according to one embodiment of the present disclosure comprises the steps of: converting parallel pipeline execution on a GPU for processing a query, into a tree traversal on a tuple processing tree; redistributing nodes on the tree to lanes within warps based on a level on the tuple processing tree within one warp set on the GPU to process a query; and redistributing at least some of the nodes on the tree of a first warp from the first warp in a busy state to a second warp in an idle state on the GPU in which a plurality of warps for processing the query are distributed.
first_claim: 1. A method of accelerating query processing utilizing a graphics processing unit (GPU), the method comprising: converting parallel pipeline execution on a GPU for processing a query into tree traversal on a tuple processing/evaluation tree; redistributing nodes of the tuple processing/evaluation tree to lanes in one warp, which is set on the GPU to process the query, based on levels in the tuple processing/evaluation tree; and redistributing at least a part of nodes of the tuple processing/evaluation tree from a first warp in a busy state to a second warp in an idle state on the GPU in which a plurality of warps for processing the query are distributed.
assignees: POSTECH RESEARCH AND BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT FOUNDATION

title: Task execution scheduling
abstract: One or more embodiments of the present disclosure relate to identifying, based on application data associated with a computing application that includes a set of runnables, a plurality of scheduling branches associated with scheduling execution of at least a subset of runnables of the set of runnables. Further, one or more embodiments relate to selecting a scheduling branch from the plurality of scheduling branches based at least on a coupling constraint that is applied to related runnables of at least the subset of runnables. The related runnables may include a first runnable that is designated for execution on a first compute engine and that triggers execution of a second runnable on a second compute engine. In addition, one or more embodiments may relate to determining an execution schedule of the set of runnables based at least on the scheduling branch.
first_claim: 1. A system comprising: one or more processing units to perform operations comprising: identifying, based at least on a compute graph associated with a computing application that includes a set of runnables, a plurality of scheduling branches associated with scheduling execution of at least a subset of runnables of the set of runnables, the plurality of scheduling branches individually including candidate execution orderings of two or more runnables of the set of runnables as determined at least from corresponding branching points in the compute graph; selecting a scheduling branch from the plurality of scheduling branches based at least on a coupling constraint that is applied to related runnables of at least the subset of runnables, wherein: the related runnables include a first runnable that is designated for execution on a first compute engine and that triggers execution of a second runnable on a second compute engine, scheduling branches that include candidate execution orderings that violate the coupling constraint are removed from consideration for selection; and the application of the coupling constraint to the related runnables ensures that the scheduling branch, as selected, maintains that the first runnable as executed on the first compute engine triggers execution of the second runnable on the second compute engine; and determining, based at least on the scheduling branch as selected, a deterministic execution schedule of the set of runnables, the deterministic execution schedule being fixed across multiple different execution iterations of the computing application.

title: Provisioning of performance states for central processing units (CPUS)
abstract: Systems, methods, and apparatuses disclosed herein can operate in different performance states that provide different energy performance tradeoffs and, in some embodiments, can dynamically switch between these different performance states. These systems, methods, and apparatuses can estimate specific timeframes that workloads are to be completed. These systems, methods, and apparatuses can identify one or more processes that are being executed to perform the workloads. These systems, methods, and apparatuses can dynamically provision one or more performance states from among these different performance states to execute the process to complete the workloads within the specific timeframes. These systems, methods, and apparatuses can dynamically provision the one or more performance states for the one or more process that optimizes power consumption and/or performance while completing the workloads within the specific timeframes.
first_claim: 1. A method for operating a Central Processing Unit (CPU), the method comprising: estimating, by the CPU, a plurality of specific timeframes that a plurality of workloads are to be completed to determine a plurality of workload completion windows; identifying, by the CPU, a process that is performing the plurality of workloads from among a plurality of processes that are being executed by the CPU over the plurality of workload completion windows; provisioning, by the CPU, a performance state from among a plurality of different performance states to execute the process to complete the plurality of workloads within the plurality of workload completion windows; determining, by the CPU, whether the plurality of workloads being performed by the process are a plurality of deadline-bound workloads; and executing, by the CPU based on determining the plurality of workloads are the deadline-bound workloads, the plurality of workloads in accordance with the performance state.

title: Routing in a GPU super-cluster
abstract: A plurality of GPU clusters are communicatively coupled with one another via a plurality of network devices arranged in a hierarchical structure, wherein the GPU clusters includes at least a first GPU cluster operating at a first speed and a second GPU cluster operating at a second speed that is different than the first speed. A routing policy is configured for each network device, wherein the configuring includes establishing a mapping of each incoming port-link of the network device to a unique outgoing port-link of the network device. For a packet transmitted by a GPU of a host machine and received by a first network device, an incoming port-link of the first network device is determined on which the packet was received and based on the configuring, an outgoing port-link is identified that corresponds to the incoming port-link. The packet is forwarded on the outgoing port-link of the network device.
first_claim: 1. A method comprising: providing a plurality of graphical processing unit (GPU) clusters, the plurality of GPU clusters being communicatively coupled with one another via a plurality of network devices that are arranged in a hierarchical structure, wherein the plurality of GPU clusters includes at least a first GPU cluster operating at a first speed and a second GPU cluster operating at a second speed that is different than the first speed; configuring a routing policy for each network device of the plurality of network devices, wherein the configuring includes establishing a mapping of each incoming port-link of the network device to a different outgoing port-link of the network device; for a packet belonging to a workload of a GPU, and transmitted by the GPU of a host machine and received by a first network device from the plurality of network devices, determining an incoming port-link of the first network device on which the packet was received; identifying based on the configuring, an outgoing port-link corresponding to the incoming port-link; and forwarding the packet on the outgoing port-link of the network device; and executing the workload of the GPU based on the configuring.

title: DECOUPLING OF VIRTUAL MACHINE HOST AND GUEST POWER USAGE
abstract: Systems and methods are provided for implementing decoupling of virtual machine host and guest power usage. An orchestrator of a computing system assigns a virtual machine (“VM”) performance level to a VM or guest for performing a VM task at a high performance level, and assigns a management partition (“MP”) performance level to the MP or host for performing a management task at a low performance level. A hypervisor of the computing system provides hardware processing resources of a central processing unit (“CPU”) core to the VM to perform the VM task, based on the high performance level, and provides hardware processing resources of another CPU core or a system agent to the MP to perform the management task, based on the low performance level, thereby adjusting the computing system to a mixed mode that is reverted to a power saver mode after performing the VM task.
first_claim: 1. A system, comprising: a processing system comprising an orchestrator, a hypervisor, and a central processing unit (“CPU”); memory coupled to the processing system, the memory comprising computer executable instructions that, when executed by the processing system, causes the system to perform operations comprising: assigning, by the orchestrator and based on first information regarding whether a virtual machine (“VM”) task to be performed by a VM is a high performance task or a low performance task, a first VM performance level to the VM for the VM task, the first VM performance level for the VM task being one of a high performance level or a low performance level; assigning, by the orchestrator and based on second information indicating that the management task is a low performance task, a management partition (“MP”) performance level to an MP of the system for the management task; selecting, by the hypervisor and based on the first VM performance level assigned by the orchestrator, a first core of the CPU, and providing, by the hypervisor, hardware processing resources of the first core to the VM to perform the VM task; selecting, by the hypervisor and based on the MP performance level assigned by the orchestrator, one of a second core or a system agent of the CPU, and providing, by the hypervisor, hardware processing resources of the one of the second core or the system agent to the MP to perform the management task; and after the VM has performed the VM task, causing, by at least one the orchestrator or the hypervisor, the first core of the CPU to revert to an energy-efficient state.

title: Method, apparatus, and system for energy efficiency and energy conservation including power and performance balancing between multiple processing elements and/or a communication bus
abstract: An apparatus, method and system is described herein for efficiently balancing performance and power between processing elements based on measured workloads. If a workload of a processing element indicates that it is a bottleneck, then its performance may be increased. However, if a platform or integrated circuit including the processing element is already operating at a power or thermal limit, the increase in performance is counterbalanced by a reduction or cap in another processing element's performance to maintain compliance with the power or thermal limit. As a result, bottlenecks are identified and alleviated by balancing power allocation, even when multiple processing elements are operating at a power or thermal limit.
first_claim: 1. An integrated circuit package comprising: a core unit having a first core including a first cache memory, a second core including a second cache memory, and a shared cache memory to be shared by at least the first core and the second core, the first and second cores each having two architecture state registers; a graphics processing unit (GPU) to execute a graphics workload; a memory controller; a cache coherent interconnect coupling the core unit and the GPU; a static random access memory; an interface to couple the integrated circuit package with another device via a Peripheral Component Interconnect Express (PCIe) protocol; a first workload monitor to determine a core workload of the core unit; a second workload monitor to determine the graphics workload of the GPU; a third workload monitor to determine a bus workload for the cache coherent interconnect; and a power controller coupled to the first, second, and third workload monitors to receive inputs therefrom and configured to balance performance of the core unit and the GPU according to actual monitored workloads of the core unit, the GPU and the cache coherent interconnect within a thermal design power (TDP) power limit for the integrated circuit package to achieve maximum performance for the integrated circuit package by: at a first time when the GPU is fully occupied, (i) increasing a frequency for the GPU, and capping or decreasing a frequency for the core unit and the cache coherent interconnect if the TDP power limit for the integrated circuit package has been reached.

title: Unified memory systems and methods
abstract: The present invention facilitates efficient and effective utilization of unified virtual addresses across multiple components. In one exemplary implementation, an address allocation process comprises: establishing space for managed pointers across a plurality of memories, including allocating one of the managed pointers with a first portion of memory associated with a first one of a plurality of processors; and performing a process of automatically managing accesses to the managed pointers across the plurality of processors and corresponding memories. The automated management can include ensuring consistent information associated with the managed pointers is copied from the first portion of memory to a second portion of memory associated with a second one of the plurality of processors based upon initiation of an accesses to the managed pointers from the second one of the plurality of processors.
first_claim: 1. One or more processors, comprising: processing circuitry to, in response to an attempt to access a pointer to data by a first processing entity, cause the data to be copied from a memory location of a second processing entity to a memory location of the first processing entity.

title: METHOD AND APPARATUS FOR SCHEDULING AND ASSIGNING TASKS TO COMPUTING RESOURCES
abstract: The disclosure relates to a method, apparatus and non-transitory computer readable media for scheduling and assigning tasks to computing resources. The method comprises receiving a list of tasks, the list of tasks including batch tasks, real-time tasks and synchronous tasks, each task being assigned a weight. The method comprises receiving computing resources specifications. The method comprises using Lagrangian relaxation for maximizing a weighted number of tasks, from the list of tasks, to be admitted according to the computing resources specifications. The method comprises preparing a plan for each of the computing resources, each plan comprising a portion of the list of tasks scheduled and assigned to the computing resource.
first_claim: 1. A computer implemented method for scheduling and assigning tasks to computing resources, comprising: receiving a list of tasks, the list of tasks including batch tasks, real-time tasks and synchronous tasks, each task being assigned a weight; receiving computing resources specifications; using Lagrangian relaxation for maximizing a weighted number of tasks, from the list of tasks, to be admitted according to the computing resources specifications; and preparing a plan for each of the computing resources, each plan comprising a portion of the list of tasks scheduled and assigned to the computing resource.

title: ELECTRONIC DEVICE COMPRISING PLURALITY OF COMPUTING NODES AND A METHOD OF OPERATING ONE OF THE PLURALITY OF COMPUTING NODES
abstract: An electronic device includes a host, and a plurality of computing nodes configured to execute a model in response to a request from the host, in which each of the plurality of computing nodes comprises a computing device configured to perform a computation of the model, a first memory device configured to store a model parameter used for the computation of the model, and a second memory device configured to assist the first memory device, and in which a first computing node among the plurality of computing nodes is configured to: determine a unit number of nodes based on a memory capacity required for storage of the model parameter and a memory capacity provided by second memory devices of the plurality of computing nodes, and group the plurality of computing nodes based on the unit number of nodes.
first_claim: 1. An electronic device comprising: a host; and a plurality of computing nodes configured to execute a large language model in response to a request from the host, wherein each of the plurality of computing nodes comprises: a computing device configured to perform a computation of the large language model, a first memory device configured to store a model parameter used for the computation of the large language model, and a second memory device configured to support the first memory device, wherein the plurality of computing nodes includes a first computing node, and wherein the first computing node is configured to: determine a unit number of nodes based on a memory capacity required for storage of the model parameter and a memory capacity provided by second memory devices of the plurality of computing nodes, and group the plurality of computing nodes based on the unit number of nodes.

title: DISTRIBUTED EDGE AI COMPUTING FABRIC WITH DEDICATED WIRELESS INTERCONNECTS FOR GPU-ENABLED WIRELESS ACCESS POINTS
abstract: In one embodiment, an illustrative method herein may comprise: receiving, at a wireless access point comprising a graphics processing unit and a high-throughput, low-latency wireless interconnect, workload metrics and connectivity metrics broadcast from a plurality of neighboring access points; dynamically selecting one or more of the plurality of neighboring access points to form a decentralized compute cluster based on the workload metrics and the connectivity metrics; partitioning an artificial intelligence workload into a plurality of task segments for execution across the decentralized compute cluster; executing, by the graphics processing unit of the wireless access point, a first subset of the plurality of task segments locally; and transmitting or receiving, over the high-throughput, low-latency wireless interconnect with the decentralized compute cluster, a second subset of the plurality of task segments using a direct GPU-to-GPU wireless data exchange that bypasses CPU-mediated data paths.
first_claim: 1. A method, comprising: receiving, at a wireless access point comprising a graphics processing unit and a high-throughput, low-latency wireless interconnect, workload metrics and connectivity metrics broadcast from a plurality of neighboring access points; dynamically selecting one or more of the plurality of neighboring access points to form a decentralized compute cluster based on the workload metrics and the connectivity metrics; partitioning an artificial intelligence workload into a plurality of task segments for execution across the decentralized compute cluster; executing, by the graphics processing unit of the wireless access point, a first subset of the plurality of task segments locally; and transmitting or receiving, over the high-throughput, low-latency wireless interconnect with the decentralized compute cluster, a second subset of the plurality of task segments using a direct GPU-to-GPU wireless data exchange that bypasses CPU-mediated data paths.

title: Address management in GPU super cluster
abstract: Described herein is a network fabric including a plurality of graphical processing unit (GPU) clusters that are communicatively coupled with one another via a plurality of switches arranged in a hierarchical structure including a first tier of switches, a second tier of switches, and a third tier of switches. One or more switches are selected from the third tier of switches to form a set of target switches, where each target switch receives address information of each GPU included in the plurality of GPU clusters. Each target switch generates, a plurality of sets of address information by filtering received address information based on a condition and transmits the plurality of sets of address information to each switch included in the first tier of switches, wherein the switch stores a subset of the plurality of sets of address information in accordance with the condition.
first_claim: 1. A method comprising: providing a plurality of graphical processing unit (GPU) clusters, the plurality of GPU clusters being communicatively coupled with one another via a plurality of switches arranged in a hierarchical structure, the hierarchical structure including: (i) a plurality of blocks of switches including a first tier of switches and a second tier of switches, and (ii) a plurality of groups of switches comprising a third tier of switches, the plurality of groups of switches communicatively coupling the plurality of blocks of switches; selecting at least one target switch from each group of switches included in the plurality of group of switches to form a set of target switches; receiving, by each target switch in the set of target switches, address information of each GPU included in the plurality of GPU clusters; generating, by each target switch in the set of target switches, a plurality of sets of address information by filtering received address information based on a condition; transmitting, by each target switch, the plurality of sets of address information to each switch included in the first tier of switches, wherein the switch stores a subset of the plurality of sets of address information in accordance with the condition; and executing a workload by the plurality of GPU clusters based on the transmitting.

title: Method and System for Reducing Deadlock and Query Management in Database
abstract: A computer-implemented method for query deployment in a database system includes receiving, by a first LSTM cell, time-series data indicating activity levels across a plurality of database nodes, and analyzing, by the first LSTM cell, the time-series data to detect one or more blocked or deadlocked queries. The method includes, evaluating, by a second LSTM cell, nodes within a database to determine if such nodes have capacity and availability to process the blocked or deadlocked queries, and if such nodes have the availability and capacity within the database, rerouting the blocked or deadlocked queries to those nodes.
first_claim: 1. A computer-implemented method for query deployment in a database system, comprising: receiving, by a first LSTM cell, time-series data indicating activity levels across a plurality of database nodes; analyzing, by the first LSTM cell, the time-series data to detect one or more blocked or deadlocked queries; responsive to the detection of blocked or deadlocked queries, evaluating, by a second LSTM cell, nodes within a database to determine whether such nodes have capacity and availability to process the blocked or deadlocked queries; responsive to a determination that such nodes within the database have the availability and capacity, rerouting the blocked or deadlocked queries to those nodes; responsive to a determination that there are no nodes within the database having capacity and availability to process the queries, searching, by the second LSTM cell, for available edge computing resources; and upon identifying available edge computing resources, rerouting the blocked or deadlocked queries to the edge computing resources.

title: Disaggregated Memory Pooling Across Commodity-DRAM Compute Sleds
abstract: Implementations address the memory demands of modern AI, machine-learning, and HPC workloads, where capacity requirements grow and shift while memory installed in individual servers remains stranded and costly to scale. A disaggregated memory system pools DRAM contributed by multiple memory-compute sleds, each carrying a small number of CPUs, DRAM components, and an RPU that performs translations, and connects the sleds to consuming entities such as accelerators and hosts through a switch. A processor monitors utilization across the sleds and dynamically allocates memory to entities as demand changes, while an RPU exposes to an entity a memory capacity larger than that of any single sled. In some implementations the pool is assembled predominantly from commodity DRAM, keeping high-density 3D stack memory to a small fraction, supporting large pooled capacity at attractive cost per gigabyte for datacenter scale-up.
first_claim: 1. A system comprising: memory-compute sleds, each comprising: no more than four central processing units (CPUs), at least 32 GB of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) components accessible within an address space utilized by the CPUs, and at least one Resource Provisioning Unit (RPU) configured to perform translations; a switch coupled to the RPUs of the memory-compute sleds and to entities; a processor configured to: monitor resource utilization across the memory-compute sleds, and dynamically allocate memory from the memory-compute sleds to the entities; and wherein the RPU is capable of exposing, to at least one of the entities, a memory capacity that exceeds a memory capacity of any individual memory-compute sled.

title: Central processing unit partition diagnosis
abstract: Systems and methods for providing cross-partition preemption analysis and prevention. Computing devices typically include a main central processing unit (CPU) with multiple cores to execute instructions independently, cooperatively, or in other suitable manners. In some examples, one or more cores are partitioned and dedicated to a particular application, where exclusive access of the cores in the partition is intended for running processes of the application. In some examples, some “noise” can be introduced in a partition, where preemptions associated with other processes can interrupt execution of the particular application. A preemption diagnostics system and method identify and prevent sources of cross-partition preemption events from running in a dedicated CPU partition. Thus, the particular application has dedicated use of the cores in the partition. As a result, latency of the application is reduced and bounded latency corresponding to a service level agreement can be achieved.
first_claim: 1. A system for preventing a cross-central processing unit (CPU) partition preemption, the system comprising: a processor; and memory storing instructions that, when executed by the processor, cause the system to: receive an indication of a preemption of a first application process running within a first CPU partition dedicated to running the first application process; determine, based on a log event associated with the preemption, a source of the preemption is a second application process different from the first application process; in response to determining the source of the preemption is the second application process, determine the preemption is a violating preemption; and in response to determining the preemption is a violating preemption, affinitize the second application process to a second CPU partition that is not dedicated to running the first application process, wherein affinitizing the second application process to the second CPU partition comprises refactoring code corresponding to the second application process such that additional preemptions associated with the second application process are assigned to the second CPU partition.

title: LARGE TO SMALL VISION-LANGUAGE MODEL RECALIBRATION
abstract: Network architectures and machine learning techniques support training a neural network of a compact vision language model (VLM) from a larger, pretrained teacher VLM. Unlike traditional knowledge distillation techniques that require student and teacher models to share an identical tokenization scheme, the network architectures and machine learning techniques disclosed herein facilitate knowledge transfer between models that implement disparate tokenization schemes.
first_claim: 1. A method for training a compact vision language model (VLM) to process multimodal input and generate textual output corresponding thereto, the method comprising: training a recalibrator neural network to align feature representations output by the compact VLM and feature representations output by a teacher VLM; and training the compact VLM, wherein training the compact VLM comprises, for one or more training iterations: obtaining sample input, the sample input comprising a textual component and a visual component; processing the sample input by the compact VLM to generate a student prediction; processing the sample input by a teacher VLM to generate a teacher prediction; generating, by the trained recalibrator neural network, a recalibrated prediction, wherein the recalibrated prediction is based, at least partially, on at least a portion of the student prediction; computing a distillation loss based on at least a portion of the recalibrated prediction and at least a portion of the teacher prediction; and updating, based at least in part on the distillation loss, parameters of the compact VLM.

title: Generating neural networks
abstract: Apparatuses, systems, and techniques to generate one or more neural networks. In at least one embodiment, one or more neural networks are generated, based on, for example, one or more convolutional neural network operations and one or more transformer neural network operations.
first_claim: 1. A processor, comprising: one or more circuits to use one or more graphics processing units (GPUs) to generate one or more neural networks based, at least in part, on: one or more convolutional neural network operations and one or more transformer neural network operations.

title: Systems and methods for large language model reasoning
abstract: A method for building an artificial intelligence (AI) agent. The method includes: receiving a training query; generating, by a first neural network based language model, a training dataset comprising a correct solution and an incorrect solution to the training query; generating, by a second neural network based language model, a first candidate score in response to the correct solution and a second candidate score in response to the incorrect solution; and training the second neural network based language model, based on a training objective. The method also includes building, at a server, an AI agent through a first application programming interface (API) to a third neural network based language model configured to generate a plurality of candidate solutions in response to the user utterance, and through a second API to the trained second neural network based language model configured to generate scores conditioned on the plurality of candidate solutions; ranking.
first_claim: 1. A method for building an artificial intelligence (AI) agent to respond to a user utterance requesting for support, comprising: receiving, via a communication interface, a training query requesting for support in natural language; generating, by a first neural network based language model, a training dataset comprising a correct solution and an incorrect solution to the training query requesting for support in response to an input prompt combining the training query requesting for support and an instruction that causes the first neural network based language model to generate the correct solution and the incorrect solution; generating, by a second neural network based language model, a first candidate score in response to the correct solution and a second candidate score in response to the incorrect solution; training, the second neural network based language model, based on a training objective comparing the first candidate score and the second candidate score; building, at a server, an AI agent through a first application programming interface (API) to a third neural network based language model, wherein the third neural network based language model generates a plurality of candidate solutions in response to the user utterance requesting for support, through a second API to the trained second neural network based language model, wherein the trained second neural network based language model generates scores conditioned on the plurality of candidate solutions, and through a third API to a fourth neural network based language model, wherein the fourth neural network based language model generates a plurality of converted candidate solutions based on the plurality of candidate solutions and the user utterance requesting for support; generating the scores conditioned on the plurality of converted candidate solutions; ranking, using the AI agent, the plurality of candidate solutions based on the scores; and generating, using the AI agent, an output solution to the user utterance requesting for support based at least in part on one or more of the ranked plurality of candidate solutions.

title: TRAINING ENGINE(S) FOR TRAINING EMBEDDING MODELS USING PRE-TRAINED TRANSFORMER-BASED MODEL ATTENTION WEIGHTS
abstract: Systems and methods herein provide a training engine and its related functions. In an aspect, a training engine may access a pre-trained large language model (LLM) with multiple layers and provide a set of domain-specific documents to the LLM. Responsive to submitting the set of domain-specific documents to the LLM, the training engine may extract attention weights from one or more layers of the LLM. Then, using the attention weights, the training engine may train an embedding model that is configured to generate vector representations for input text in the specific domain. The attention weights, which may be extracted from one or more intermediate layers of the LLM, may be used as supervision signals to train the embedding model through contrastive learning, allowing the embedding model to learn semantic relationships between text segments based on the LLM's understanding of the domain.
first_claim: 1. A computing apparatus comprising: a computer-readable storage media comprising processor-executable instructions stored thereon; and a processor coupled to the computer-readable storage media and configured to execute the processor-executable instructions that, when executed by the processor, direct the computing apparatus to at least: provide a set of domain-specific documents to a pre-trained large language model (LLM), wherein the LLM comprises a plurality of layers; extract attention weights from one or more layers of the plurality of layers of the LLM; and train an embedding model using the extracted attention weights, wherein the embedding model is configured to generate vector representations for input text in the specific domain.

title: SYSTEMS AND METHODS FOR A VISION-LANGUAGE PRETRAINING FRAMEWORK
abstract: Embodiments described herein provide a multimodal vision-language model. The multimodal vision-language model contains a Generalist Multimodal Transformer capable of complete multiple tasks using the same set of parameters learning from pre-training. The Generalist Multimodal Transformer allows alignment between frozen, unimodal encoders, such as image encoders and large language models. The Generalist Multimodal Transformer eliminates the need for fine-tuning the image encoders and large language models.
first_claim: 1. A method for a multimodal framework for answering a question relating to an image, the method comprising: receiving, from a communication interface, an input image and a textual prompt instructing a task relating to the input image; encoding, by an image encoder of the multimodal framework, the input image into an image representation; applying, by an attention module of the multimodal framework, cross-attention between the image representation and a set of learnable query vector to transform visual features into a transformed representation; generating, by a pretrained language model of the multimodal framework, a combined representation based on the transformed representation and the textual prompt; and generating, by the pretrained language model as a decoder, a text response based on the combined representation.

title: AGENT-BASED ARCHITECTURES FOR CONTENT VALIDATION
abstract: Systems and methods described herein relate to agent-based architectures for automated content validation. Multiple first software agents are executed to generate individual comparison data based on comparing at least first content and second content according to respective comparison metrics. At least one second software agent is executed to generate overall comparison data based on the individual comparison data. Machine learning model operations are controlled using the overall comparison data and the first content or the second content.
first_claim: 1. One or more processors comprising processing circuitry to perform operations comprising: executing a plurality of first artificial intelligence (AI) agents to generate individual comparison data based at least on a comparison between first content and second content according to a respective comparison metric; executing at least one second AI agent to generate overall comparison data based at least on the individual comparison data generated using the plurality of first AI agents; and controlling machine learning model operations using the overall comparison data and at least one of the first content or the second content.

title: Graph-based recurrence classification machine learning frameworks
abstract: Various embodiments of the present invention provide methods, apparatus, systems, computing devices, computing entities, and/or the like for performing predictive data analysis operations. For example, certain embodiments of the present invention utilize systems, methods, and computer program products that perform predictive data analysis operations by using a graph-based recurrence classification machine learning framework that includes a graph neural network machine learning model and a recurrence classification machine learning model, where the recurrence classification machine learning model is configured to generate a predicted recurrence classification based at least in part on one or more graph-based features generated by a graph neural network machine learning model and one or more entity features associated with an entity identifier for an incoming event.
first_claim: 1. A computer-implemented method comprising: identifying, by one or more processors, a graph data object comprising a plurality of graph nodes and a graph edge connecting at least two of the plurality of graph nodes, wherein: (i) the plurality of graph nodes comprises an event node and a characterization node, and (ii) the graph edge defines an event characterization link that connects the event node to the characterization node; determining, by the one or more processors, an updated graph data object by integrating an incoming event node associated with an incoming event into the graph data object; extracting, by the one or more processors and based at least in part on the updated graph data object, an individualized subgraph comprising a subset of the plurality of graph nodes that is within a threshold value of graph edges from the incoming event node, wherein the threshold value of graph edges is defined by a hyperparameter of a machine learning framework; generating, by the one or more processors and the machine learning framework, and based at least in part on the individualized subgraph, a predicted recurrence classification for the incoming event by: (i) generating, using a graph neural network of the machine learning framework, a plurality of graph-based features from the individualized subgraph, and (ii) generating, using a recurrence classification model of the machine learning framework, the predicted recurrence classification based at least in part on the plurality of graph-based features, wherein the graph neural network and the recurrence classification model of the machine learning framework are trained end-to-end using a training dataset, the training dataset comprising a training entry comprising a label and a training individualized subgraph for a training event node within the graph data object, the training entry being generated by: (a) generating, based on the graph data object, the label for the training event node within the graph data object, and (b) in response to generating the label for the training event node, extracting the training individualized subgraph for the training event node based at least in part on the hyperparameter; and initiating, by the one or more processors, a performance of one or more prediction-based actions based at least in part on the predicted recurrence classification.

title: Neural architecture search
abstract: Methods, systems, and apparatus, including computer programs encoded on computer storage media, for determining neural network architectures. One of the methods includes generating, using a controller neural network, a batch of output sequences, each output sequence in the batch defining a respective architecture of a child neural network that is configured to perform a particular neural network task; for each output sequence in the batch: training a respective instance of the child neural network having the architecture defined by the output sequence; evaluating a performance of the trained instance of the child neural network on the particular neural network task to determine a performance metric for the trained instance of the child neural network on the particular neural network task; and using the performance metrics for the trained instances of the child neural network to adjust the current values of the controller parameters of the controller neural network.
first_claim: 1. A method performed by one or more computers, comprising: determining, using a controller, a plurality of respective architectures of a child neural network that is configured to perform a particular neural network task; for each respective architecture in the plurality of respective architectures: training an instance of the child neural network having the respective architecture on training data that includes a plurality of training inputs each associated with a respective target training output to perform the particular neural network task; and after the training, determining, based on evaluating a performance of the trained instance of the child neural network using validation data that includes one or more different training inputs than the training data, a performance metric for the trained instance of the child neural network on the particular neural network task; and using the performance metrics for the trained instances of the child neural network to adjust the controller.

title: Method for reducing element of neural network having attention mechanism
abstract: A method including: inserting padding layers into a downstream side of each of a Q layer and a K layer, the padding layer padding one or more elements of a tensor, the Q and K layers respectively outputting a Query and a Key, the Query and the Key being a result of an arithmetic operating process on an input tensor in an attention mechanism in the trained machine learning model of a neural network having the attention mechanism, and padding a tensor QT and a tensor KT with the padding layers associated one with each of a reduced Q layer and a reduced K layer such that the tensor QT and the tensor KT have a same number of elements, the tensor QT and the tensor KT being respectively included in the reduced Q layer and the reduced K layer in which one or more elements are reduced.
first_claim: 1. A non-transitory computer-readable recording medium having stored therein a machine learning program for causing a computer to execute a process comprising: inserting padding layers into a downstream side of each of a Q layer and a K layer, each of the padding layers padding one or more elements of a tensor, the Q layer outputting a Query, the K layer outputting a Key, the Query and the Key being a result of an arithmetic operating process on an input tensor in an attention mechanism in the trained machine learning model of a neural network having the attention mechanism, and padding a tensor QT included in a reduced Q layer in which one or more elements are reduced based on a first reduction ratio and a tensor KT included in a reduced K layer in which one or more elements are reduced based on a second reduction ratio with the padding layers associated one with each of the reduced Q layer and the reduced K layer such that the tensor QT has a number of elements same as a number of elements that the tensor KT has.

title: COMPUTER-IMPLEMENTED METHOD AND SET-UP FOR CONFIGURING AN IMAGING AND/OR IMAGE-PROCESSING DEVICE
abstract: The computer-implemented method for the automatable setting-up of a device intended for a predefined use is characterised in that the method is effected by means of a set-up assistant which has a large language model and is based on generative artificial intelligence, wherein the method comprises the following steps: a user communicating with the configuration assistant in natural language, via a computer interface, in order to acquire data relating to the predefined intended use; training a set-up model on the basis of the acquired data or optimising an existing set-up model on the basis of the acquired data; providing, via the computer interface, a previously trained, transformer-based set-up model, which comprises at least one transformer component; prompting the retraining of the previously trained, transformer-based set-up model, using the training data based on the acquired data; releasing the trained, transformer-based set-up model for the automatable setting-up of the device.
first_claim: 1. Computer-implemented method for the automatable setting-up of at least one imaging and/or image-processing device intended for a predefined use, characterised in that the method is effected by means of a set-up assistant which has a large language model and is based on generative artificial intelligence, wherein the method comprises the following steps: training a transformer-based set-up model (450) on the basis of operation-relevant and/or product-relevant data (425) of the at least one imaging and/or image-processing device or optimising an existing transformer-based set-up model on the basis of such data; providing, via a computer interface (430), the trained or optimised transformer-based set-up model (450), which comprises at least one transformer component; a user communicating (440) with the set-up assistant (400) in natural language, via the computer interface (430), in order to acquire data (435) relating to the predefined intended use of the at least one imaging and/or image-processing device; prompting (445) the trained, transformer-based set-up model (450), using the acquired data for the predefined intended use, to output optimised set-up data (455); releasing (445) the optimised set-up data (455) output by the trained, transformer-based set-up model (450) for the automatable setting-up of the at least one imaging and/or image-processing device (300-310, 415).

title: System and method for accurate responses from chatbots and LLMs
abstract: Systems and methods are described for obtaining accurate responses from large language models (LLMs) and chatbots, including for question and answering, exposition, and summarization. These systems and methods accomplish these objectives via use of noun phrase avoiding processes such as a noun phrase collision detection process, a query splitting process, and a topical splitting process as well as by use of formatted facts, formatted fact model correction interfaces (FF MCIs), bounded-scope deterministic (BSD) neural networks, processes and methods, and intelligent storage and retrieval (ISAR) systems and methods. These systems and methods avoid and bypass noun phrase collisions and correct for errors caused by noun phrase collisions so that hallucinations are eliminated from LLM responses.
first_claim: 1. A system for correcting AI hallucinations, the system comprising: at least one response from a large language model (“LLM”); at least one external knowledge source; at least one self-containment process; at least one retriever process that comprises two inputs; wherein one of the two inputs comprises a collection of standalone statements and wherein the other of the two inputs comprises a provided standalone statement; and wherein the at least one retriever process returns at least one standalone statement from the collection of standalone statements that most closely matches the provided standalone statement; wherein the at least one external knowledge source is converted into at least one external knowledge collection of standalone statements using the at least one self-containment process; wherein the at least one response from the LLM is converted into at least one LLM-response standalone statement using the at least one self-containment process; wherein a closest matching standalone statement for the at least one LLM-response standalone statement is found within the at least one external knowledge collection of standalone statements using the at least one retriever process; and wherein the at least one LLM-response standalone statement is replaced with the closest matching standalone statement.

title: OPTIMIZING VIRAL CAPSIDS USING MACHINE LEARNING
abstract: Methods, systems, and apparatus, including computer programs encoded on a computer storage medium, for generating a fitness score for a capsid monomer.
