In one aspect, a method comprises: receiving data defining an amino acid sequence of a monomer of a capsid; processing the data defining the amino acid sequence of the monomer of the capsid using an embedding neural network, in accordance with values of a set of embedding neural network parameters, to generate an embedding of the monomer of the capsid; processing the embedding of the monomer of the capsid using a fitness prediction machine learning model to generate a fitness score that characterizes a predicted quality of the capsid; and outputting the fitness score that characterizes the predicted quality of the capsid.
first_claim: 1. A method comprising: receiving data defining an amino acid sequence of a monomer of a capsid; processing the data defining the amino acid sequence of the monomer of the capsid using an embedding neural network, in accordance with values of a set of embedding neural network parameters, to generate an embedding of the monomer of the capsid; processing the embedding of the monomer of the capsid using a fitness prediction machine learning model to generate a fitness score that characterizes a predicted quality of the capsid; and outputting the fitness score that characterizes the predicted quality of the capsid.

title: Neural network-based context-aware code translation and optimization
abstract: Systems and methods for efficiently translating program code from a source language to a target language. Input source code is parsed, using a processor device, into an Intermediate Representation (IR). A structural and semantic model of the source code are established by applying static analysis to the IR, and a program skeleton of the target code is constructed from the IR, including generating context-aware placeholders. The IR is transformed into a Single Static Assignment (SSA) form, and a System Dependency Graph (SDG) is built from the SSA form. The SDG is traversed to order translation tasks, and ordered tasks are translated into the target language using a Large Language Model (LLM). A translated program is generated by integrating translated code segments into a coherent program structure in the target language.
first_claim: 1. A method for efficiently translating program code from a source language to a target language, comprising: parsing, using a processor device, input source code into an Intermediate Representation (IR); establishing a structural and semantic model of the source code by applying static analysis to the IR; constructing a program skeleton of a target code from the IR, including generating context-aware placeholders filled with contextually relevant translations; transforming the IR into a Single Static Assignment (SSA) form and building a System Dependency Graph (SDG) from the SSA form; traversing the SDG to order basic blocks, and populating a dynamic SDG stack with the basic blocks; translating the basic blocks into the target language using a Large Language Model (LLM) with the context-aware placeholders to guide the LLM in generating functionally equivalent code; wherein the translating the basic blocks into the target language includes adapting the translated code segments to conform to runtime constraints of a target computing environment to enable execution of the translated program within the target environment and further adapting the translated code segments to meet specific additional performance metrics and resource constraints of a target computing environment, including one or more of memory usage, processing speed, and integration with existing software infrastructure; and generating a translated program by integrating translated code segments into a coherent program structure in the target language.

title: METHODS FOR OPERATING A BIOLOGICAL NEURAL NETWORK COMPUTING SYSTEM WITH ADAPTIVE COMPUTATIONAL INTERFACES AND AUTOMATED CONTROL
abstract: An automation system is disclosed that couples an in vitro biological neural network (BNN) to a closed-loop control architecture including a stimulation interface, a readout interface, a supply interface, and a sensing interface. The BNN comprises neural cells in contact with a culture medium supported, for example, on a microelectrode array substrate, a hydrogel, a microfluidic device, or a combination thereof. The stimulation unit applies electrical, optical, optogenetic, mechanical, or field-based stimulation to the neural cells, and the readout unit records neural activity using, for example, microelectrode arrays, patch-clamp, optical or chemical sensors. The supply unit delivers a controllable amount of chemical or biological agents, such as nutrients, neuromodulators, growth factors, drugs, extracellular vesicles, ions, or gases, into the culture medium. The sensing unit measures at least one physical, chemical, or biological state parameter of the in vitro biological neural network, including parameters from the cell culture medium from the neural cells, or from the cell culture environment, such as temperature, pH, osmolality, optical properties, nutrients, metabolites, nucleic acids, inflammatory or immune factors, and misfolded or aggregated protein species. An automation controller, optionally implementing a machine learning model and/or an artificial intelligence agent, receives the readout signal and/or the measured state parameter, compares them with predetermined reference values, and adjusts stimulation parameters and/or supply-unit delivery amount and timing to modulate the activity, metabolism, and learning behavior of the BNN. Corresponding methods are provided for regulating the functional or physiological state of a BNN by iteratively stimulating the neural cells, delivering agents, measuring neural readout signals and/or physical, chemical or biological state parameters, comparing them to references, and updating stimulation signals and/or supply amounts and/or supply delivery timing according to the comparison results.
first_claim: 1. A system comprising a biological neural network (BNN) comprising an in vitro culture of neural cells and a culture medium in contact with the neural cell culture; a stimulation interface configured to apply a stimulation signal to the biological neural network; a readout interface configured to measure a readout signal representative of the biological neural network activity; a supply interface configured to deliver a controllable amount of a chemical or biological agent to the neural cell culture; a sensing interface configured to measure at least one biological, chemical, or physical state parameter of the biological neural network; and an automation controller operably coupled to the stimulation interface, the readout interface, the supply interface, and the sensing interface, wherein the automation controller is configured to determine a control action based on one or more of (i) the measured readout signal and (ii) the measured state parameter, and to apply the control action through one or more of the stimulation interface and the supply interface to regulate a physiological or functional state of the biological neural network.

title: Generating a multi-entity graph representation for determining a therapeutic treatment utilizing a graph neural network
abstract: The present disclosure relates to methods, systems, and non-transitory computer-readable media for utilizing novel multi-entity graph representations and a graph neural network to determine therapeutic treatments for clinical patients and/or to select preclinical models that are representative of a patient population. In particular, the disclosed systems can access (or receive) data from a plurality of data sources, including digital clinical datasets, functional response machine learning embeddings, and/or digital preclinical-model datasets. Based on this data, the disclosed systems may generate a multi-entity graph representation that includes a plurality of nodes corresponding to a plurality of data entity types (e.g., clinical patients, genes, compounds, and/or preclinical models) and a plurality of edges that connect the plurality of nodes. In some cases, the disclosed systems generate embeddings (e.g., node embeddings) in a latent space utilizing the graph neural network and compare the embeddings to determine a therapeutic treatment and/or select a preclinical model.
first_claim: 1. A computer-implemented method comprising: generating a multi-entity graph representation comprising nodes and edges by: generating a first plurality of nodes for a plurality of clinical patients from a digital clinical dataset; generating a second plurality of nodes for a plurality of genes; generating a third plurality of nodes comprising at least one of: compound nodes for a plurality of compounds or preclinical model nodes for a plurality of preclinical models from a digital preclinical-model dataset; and generating a plurality of edges by encoding relationships between the nodes into the edges, wherein generating the plurality of edges comprises generating a gene-gene edge between gene nodes of the second plurality of nodes representing genes from cells exposed to a perturbation by: generating, utilizing a machine learning model, functional response machine learning embeddings for genes corresponding to the gene nodes, the functional response machine learning embeddings comprising one or more phenomic embeddings or transcriptomic embeddings; and generating the gene-gene edge between the gene nodes by determining a similarity measure between the functional response machine learning embeddings; generating, utilizing a graph neural network and from the multi-entity graph representation, embeddings in a shared latent space, wherein the embeddings comprise a clinical patient embedding and at least one of: a compound embedding, a preclinical model embedding, a gene embedding, or an additional clinical patient embedding; and comparing the clinical patient embedding and at least one of the compound embedding, the preclinical model embedding, the gene embedding, or the additional clinical patient embedding to determine a therapeutic treatment for one or more patients of the plurality of clinical patients.
